answer: Unique-Answer Chit Registration. Each identity must submit an answer to a freshly generated, one-time puzzle whose solution is bound to a hidden ivory key; the registry accepts only the first valid submission seen, so a copied or replanted answer is discarded before scoring. Duplicate agents routing through the same grove of relays are detected because their reused solutions collide. An attacker pays one full generation cost—compute plus puzzle procurement—per identity, since each fresh pearl of a solution cannot be recycled or resold.
